history.dynasty: Chalukya (main temple attributed to the Chalukyas); renovated by the Kakatiyas in the 12th-13th century
history.period: Ancient - mentioned in the Skanda Purana; Chalukya-built, Kakatiya renovation 12th-13th century (per a South Indian History Congress study - verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the generic 'Mukteshwara Swamy Temple [Karimnagar]' best matches the famous Kaleshwaram Kaleshwara-Mukteswara Swamy Temple - which is NOT in Karimnagar town. It stands at Kaleshwaram village in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district (postal area Mahadevpur), about 125 km from Karimnagar (per the South Indian History Congress study), at the Triveni Sangamam - the confluence of the Godavari and Pranahita rivers with the unseen Saraswati/Antarvahini - near the Maharashtra-Chhattisgarh-Telangana border trijunction. Identity certainty: HIGH - this is the best-supported referent for a 'Mukteshwara' shrine in this region. It is one of the Trilinga Kshetrams (with Srisailam and Draksharamam/Draksharamam Bhimeswaram). The unique feature: two lingas - Shiva as Mukteswara and Yama as Kaleshwara - share a single pedestal (Skanda Purana: Yama performed penance and was granted a place beside Shiva). The Mukteswara linga has two 'nostrils'; water poured in them disappears and is believed to merge with the Godavari. Legends: a Vaishya's abhisheka with hundreds of milk pots manifested at the sangam (hence 'Dakshina Gangotri'); the Nagpur king Bhonsle's test of the nostrils; Vishwakarma's Yama Gundam tank (holy dip = blessings of many holy waters); Jaya-Vijaya as door-keepers. Dravidian architecture with carved pillars and halls; a fish sculpture is iconic. Ashta Tirthas lie along the Godavari here. Documented with the corrected town and district.

name: Mukteshwara Swamy Temple
town: Kaleshwaram (CSV town 'Karimnagar' is WRONG - the temple is at Kaleshwaram village in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district, ~125 km from Karimnagar, at the Godavari-Pranahita confluence)
town_description: Kaleshwaram is an ancient pilgrimage village in Jayashankar Bhupalpally district (Mahadevpur postal area) at the exact merging point of the Pranahita into the Godavari - the Triveni Sangamam (Dakshina Gangotri). About 277 km from Hyderabad, 125 km from Karimnagar and 115 km from Warangal, it sits near the meeting point of Telangana, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh. One of the Trilinga Kshetrams, it is surrounded by lush greenery on the Godavari bank.
